content.title: The great debate: Does God exist?
content.description: Examine the dispute over God, evidence and the foundations of logic, science and morality.

claim.text: Bahnsen argues that reasoning presupposes the Christian God. Stein challenges the evidence for God and disputes Bahnsen’s account of the basis of logic and inquiry.

content.hinge: Does an argument establish the conditions needed for reasoning, or assume the conclusion it aims to prove?
prompts: Write out the premises behind each claim about logic.
Distinguish using reason from explaining why reasoning is reliable.
Follow both cross-examinations before assessing the argument.

content.transcriptCoverage: 42-page transcript with speeches, questioning, closing statements and audience questions. Third-party-hosted copy; the remastered recording and its subtitles have not been checked word for word.

reviews.scope: Transcript source, event identity, editorial summary, coverage notes and YouTube metadata review
reviews.note: Checked linked transcript structures and publisher notices; compared participant/event descriptions with the recording listings. Verified YouTube metadata and runtimes on 2026-10-11; rejected a 9:12 Concept of God excerpt and selected the 1:31:47 debate. Summaries are editorial paraphrases. Full recordings were not watched or heard, and word-for-word alignment and whole-event completeness remain unverified. No external transcript body is republished. Existing doctrinal policy is unchanged.
